gates.detail: Example sentence capitals/punctuation and contains the word.

The example sentence 'finally managed to succeed in playing' is redundant and awkward: 'managed to' and 'succeed' mean the same thing, so it is a poor model for learners.; 'win' is not a true synonym of 'succeed'; it only overlaps in competitive contexts. Likewise, 'lose' is mainly the antonym of 'win', not of 'succeed'.; 'achieve' and 'accomplish' need an object ('achieve a goal'), whereas 'succeed' does not, so they cannot be swapped in directly. Learners may produce errors like 'Fatima finally achieved.'; The difficulty label 'Advanced' seems high for a common word like 'succeed' at ages 10-13.

issues: The example sentence 'finally managed to succeed in playing' is redundant and awkward: 'managed to' and 'succeed' mean the same thing, so it is a poor model for learners.
'win' is not a true synonym of 'succeed'; it only overlaps in competitive contexts. Likewise, 'lose' is mainly the antonym of 'win', not of 'succeed'.
'achieve' and 'accomplish' need an object ('achieve a goal'), whereas 'succeed' does not, so they cannot be swapped in directly. Learners may produce errors like 'Fatima finally achieved.'
The difficulty label 'Advanced' seems high for a common word like 'succeed' at ages 10-13.
suggested_fixes: Rewrite the example as: 'After weeks of practice, Fatima finally succeeded in playing the whole tune on her harmonium.'
Replace 'win' with 'do well' or 'prosper', and remove 'lose' or replace it with 'fall short'.
Add a note that 'achieve' and 'accomplish' need an object (e.g. 'achieve your goal'), or replace one of them with 'make it'.
